name: Somatrogon
lead: Somatrogon (MOD-4023; brand name Ngenla) is a long-acting recombinant human growth hormone analogue given by subcutaneous injection once a week. In the United States it is indicated for children aged 3 years and older with growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone [9][8].

In phase 3 trials, weekly somatrogon was compared with daily somatropin in prepubertal children with growth hormone deficiency (GHD), including a 12-month open-label randomised study and a study in Japanese children [1][2]. Reviews of the three long-acting growth hormones (lonapegsomatropin, somatrogon and somapacitan) describe non-inferior height velocity and similar safety profiles to daily growth hormone in 52-week trials [4].
It is a prescription medicine for diagnosed deficiency. No study has tested it for height gain in children without a diagnosed deficiency.

paras: The US label indicates somatrogon for pediatric patients aged 3 years and older with growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone [9]. A phase 3 study in children born small for gestational age or with idiopathic short stature is registered and recruiting [10].

According to the label, somatrogon binds the growth hormone receptor and activates the STAT5b signalling pathway, increasing serum IGF-1; GH and IGF-1 then drive metabolic changes and linear growth [9].

The US labels for long-acting growth hormones list warnings including increased mortality in acute critical illness, severe hypersensitivity, increased risk of neoplasms (notably second neoplasms in childhood cancer survivors), glucose intolerance and diabetes mellitus, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism and hypothyroidism [9]. Label pregnancy information notes that no human data are available, and that rat reproduction studies showed no embryo-fetal toxicity [9].

A 12-month phase 3 trial randomised prepubertal children with GHD to weekly somatrogon or daily somatropin and reported on efficacy and safety [1]; a Japanese phase 3 study in 44 prepubertal children made a similar comparison with daily Genotropin [2][12]. A treatment-burden study compared weekly and daily injections from the patient perspective [6][11]. A five-year open-label extension of a phase 2 dose-finding study has been published [5]. A systematic review and a network meta-analysis compared long-acting with daily growth hormone [3][7].
Post-marketing surveillance in Korea and a special investigation in Japan are registered [14][15].

timeline.event: Phase 3 trial of MOD-4023 in children with GHD starts [13].

card.summary: A weekly prescription growth hormone for children with diagnosed GH deficiency; no evidence for height gain without a deficiency.
card.note: Prescription drug for diagnosed GHD; trials are in children with deficiency only.

quick.overview:
Somatrogon (Ngenla) is a once-weekly growth hormone injection approved in the US for children aged 3 and older whose bodies do not make enough growth hormone. Phase 3 trials compared it with daily somatropin.

Trials involve children with a diagnosed deficiency. No study has tested it for height in children without one.
quick.mechanism: It binds the growth hormone receptor, activates STAT5b signalling and raises IGF-1, promoting linear growth.
quick.risks: The label lists warnings such as neoplasm risk, glucose intolerance, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism, hypothyroidism and hypersensitivity. It is prescription-only.
